en.title: Demonstratives: this and that
en.summary: This and these point to what is near; that and those point to what is far.

paragraphs: Demonstratives point to things. This and these point to what is near the speaker, and that and those point to what is far. Near and far can mean place, but they can also mean time or feeling. This morning means today, but that morning means a day in the past.

English demonstratives change for number only: this and these, that and those. They have no gender and no case. They can stand before a noun or on their own as pronouns. When they stand before a noun, we use no other determiner: this book, not the this book.

sections.title: On the telephone and in introductions

paragraphs: We use this to introduce people and to say who is calling: This is my friend Ana. Hello, this is Tom. We use that to ask who is calling: Who is that?
That can show distance in feeling as well as place: I don't like that man. This can add interest in a story: So this man comes in and sits down.

ro.title: Demonstrativele: acesta și acela
ro.summary: Cuvintele „acesta” și „acela” arată obiecte sau persoane aflate aproape sau departe de vorbitor.

paragraphs: Demonstrativele sunt cuvinte care arată obiecte sau persoane. Cuvântul „acesta” arată ceva aflat aproape de noi. Cuvântul „acela” arată ceva aflat departe de noi. Ele își schimbă forma după gen și număr.

Forma demonstrativului depinde de gen și de număr. La masculin și feminin avem cuvinte diferite. Aceste cuvinte pot sta singure sau lângă un substantiv. În fața substantivului folosim formele scurte: acest sau acel.
